commit: b1ba466f on branch mastertune-v12-diag (worktree /home/user/work/deluge-diag, based on v12 f89b478c)
timing: Measured with OSTM0: 33.33 MHz, free-running, started by the TaskManager and only read here. Uint32 differences survive the overflow every 129 s; other timers stay untouched. The v12 audio routine sits unchanged in routineUnmeasured(); routine() only wraps it (without stem export and nested calls). Load = time ÷ generated samples (audioSampleTimer). The peak applies per call (1–2 blocks, from 16 samples), not per single block; that way the DSP machine code stays untouched.
overhead: Switched off: 3 instructions and a tail call per call. Switched on: 2 timer reads per call, one task every 50 ms, 2 OLED transfers and 1 SysEx message (43 B) per second. No allocation, seqlock without blocking.
ui: Settings → CPU monitor (7-segment "CPU"), off after the device is switched on. On the OLED an inverted bottom line lies over the finished image, refreshed twice per second, e.g. "C43/71% V24 D0 S2.4/9". The screens themselves stay unchanged, but the line covers their bottom line. On the 7-segment display "C 43" appears briefly every 2 s.
sysexFormat: F0 00 21 7B 01 10 + 36 bytes + F7, 7-bit groups, LSB first, saturated. Fields: version, sequence number, window ms, CPU mean/peak (0.1%), voices now/max, direness max/share, culling, SD count/mean/max µs, max audio gap µs, samples. It is sent only to USB port 3, never to DIN, and only when there is enough room in the send buffer. Docs: cpu_stats_core.h and README.
tests: tests/cpu_stats/run.sh: the collector with a simulated timer, overflow included, is accurate to ±0.2%. The OLED line stays ≤21 characters with 200k random values. 503 SysEx messages make the round trip in Node with the decoder extracted from the page; faulty ones are rejected. compare_elf.py (v12 against diag): the audio routine and DSP functions have the same instructions, only addresses are shifted. Tables are identical or differ only in pointers. No compiler warnings.
notes: Page: tools/cpu_monitor.html. Not tested on hardware: the OLED line, the 7-segment popup and Web MIDI need the live test on the Deluge. tests/cpu_stats is not yet entered in run_all.sh. The baseline ELF for the comparison is in /home/user/work/diag-v12-base.elf. Nothing was committed in the repo /home/user/deluge.

problems.problem: The "Culling" counter also counts calls in which no voice is cut. It can therefore be far too high.
problems.evidence: It counts whenever bestVoice != nullptr and stopFrom == nullptr. But the SOFT case (line 336-339) does nothing if the chosen voice is already in FAST_RELEASE with an increment >= SOFT_CULL_INCREMENT. getPriorityRating rates later envelope stages higher (voice.cpp:3327), so SOFT and FORCE pick the same fading voice again and again. With <=7 voices and overload, line 477 runs on every render: that can give dozens of counts per second although nothing is cut. With hard culling in the FORCE loop (line 445), the same voice can also be counted several times.
problems.fix: Move the call of cpu_stats::voiceCulled() (with the condition stopFrom==nullptr) into the switch branches and only count when the voice really changes: for SOFT in the if block before doFastRelease, for FORCE only if envelopes[0].state was < FAST_RELEASE before, for HARD always. cullVoice is not DSP code, so the instruction comparison of the audio routine stays valid.

problems.problem: The SD read time (mean/max) includes the audio render time that occurs during the read. It therefore rises with the CPU load and mixes up SD and CPU bottlenecks.
problems.evidence: disk_read_without_streaming_first waits in yieldingRoutineWithTimeoutForSD (drivers/sd/sd.c:75, sdhi/userdef/sd_dev_low.c:1116). During this time the TaskManager runs the audio task (priority 0) and other tasks. So now()-startTime is wall-clock time including the rendering. Example: at 70% audio load an SD access of 2 ms shows up as about 6 ms. So the measured value does not tell whether the card is slow.
problems.fix: Keep a running counter uint64_t totalBusyTicks_ in the collector that is incremented in routineDone and never reset. clusterLoaded(startTime, busyAtStart) subtracts the increase. That gives a pure SD time next to the wall-clock latency, and both are sent (append the field at the end; the decoder accepts longer payloads). At the least, the README and the page should say "latency incl. audio".

commit: d0d03dcc (replaced commit b1ba466f on branch mastertune-v12-diag in the worktree /home/user/work/deluge-diag by amend; one patch against v12 f89b478c)
timing: As before, OS timer 0 (33.33 MHz, free-running and only read) measures every call of AudioEngine::routine(). New: the collector keeps the running sum busyTotal_ (uint32, never reset, differences safe against overflow). It is read before and after every cluster read (cpu_stats::readStart/clusterLoaded). The card time is then the wall-clock time minus the audio rendering during the read (clamped at 0). The wall-clock latency is kept as a separate value.
overhead: Still small. With the monitor off, it costs one flag check per audio call and, per cluster read, one timer read and one load. With it on, one addition per call is added, and the SysEx message has 51 instead of 43 bytes. compare_elf against v12: routineUnmeasured is identical to routine() from v12, and all DSP functions and DSP tables are the same. Only measurement points changed (cullVoice, loadCluster etc.), plus the helper countCulledVoice.
ui: For the SD value the OLED now shows the card time without audio (S2.4/9). The page cpu_monitor.html has two tiles: "SD card mean / max" and "SD latency incl. audio". The CSV has the columns sd_card_* and sd_latency_incl_audio_* for them, and the explanations of culling and SD are updated.
sysexFormat: F0 00 21 7B 01 10 + 44 bytes + F7, format 2. The fields of format 1 stay unchanged (SD mean/max = wall clock). Added at the end: SD card without audio mean (4 bytes) and max (4 bytes), in µs, as 7-bit groups with the least significant byte first. The decoder still reads format 1; the card fields are then zero.
tests: tests/cpu_stats/run.sh runs green. New testSdCardTime: the read as in the firmware, with the render time overflowing during it, and the edge case "audio > wall clock" gives 0. The OLED line takes the card values. All 503 SysEx messages make the round trip with the page's decoder without errors. Newly checked: format 1 is still read, and messages that are too short are rejected. No PC test covers the culling counter; I checked it in the code.
notes:
Culling is now counted only in the switch branches, and only when a call of the CPU protection (stopFrom==nullptr) really changes a voice:
- SOFT: in the if block, but not for voices that are already OFF.
- FORCE: if the voice was below FAST_RELEASE before or is removed.
- HARD: always.
So every voice counts once. Nothing changes in how voices are chosen.

The earlier "clean" builds only deleted build/Release; the object files stayed. This time I also deleted build/CMakeFiles/deluge.dir/Release. Twice all 356 object files were recompiled, both times with the same SHA-256 and without warnings; only the known RWX linker message appears, as in v12. In the worktree dbt only builds with DBT_NO_SYNC=1.
